joint_trait_diversification_models.summary: Models incorporating both trait change and state-dependent speciation/extinction rates to avoid biases in ancestral reconstruction (p. 104).

phylogenetic_taxonomy.label: Taxonomy in a Phylogenetic Framework
phylogenetic_taxonomy.summary: The system of naming groups (taxa) based on common descent.

phylogenetic_nomenclature.label: Phylogenetic Nomenclature (PhyloCode)
phylogenetic_nomenclature.summary: An integrated set of rules governing naming based on common descent, utilizing specifiers (p. 107).

clade_definitions.label: Clade Definitions
clade_definitions.summary: Algorithmic ways to tie a name to a specific clade on the tree.

node_based_def.label: Node-based Definition
node_based_def.summary: Definition of a clade as the most recent common ancestor of two internal specifiers and all its descendants (p. 107).

stem_based_def.label: Stem-based Definition
stem_based_def.summary: Definition of a clade as all organisms more closely related to an internal specifier than to an external specifier (p. 107).

apomorphy_based_def.label: Apomorphy-based Definition
apomorphy_based_def.summary: Definition of a clade based on the possession of a specific derived character (apomorphy) (p. 107).

taxonomy.label: Taxonomy
taxonomy.summary: The discipline concerned with identifying significant groups of organisms (taxa) and assigning scientific names to facilitate communication.

historical_taxonomy.label: Historical Taxonomy (Linnaean System)
historical_taxonomy.summary: Early systems of classification focused on ordering the natural world based on static attributes and ecological factors.

linnaean_system_facts.label: Linnaean System Details
linnaean_system_facts.summary: Specific components of the system proposed by Carl Linnaeus.
linnaean_system_facts.details: Linnaeus proposed a system of ranked categories (taxonomy) and a system of rules for naming (nomenclature). He recognized five ranks from species to class and introduced binomial nomenclature: a two-part name consisting of a genus name and a species epithet. (p. 107)

nomenclatural_codes.label: Nomenclatural Codes
nomenclatural_codes.summary: Formalized rules governing the naming of different biological groups.
nomenclatural_codes.details: Separate codes exist for bacteria (BC), plants (ICBN), and animals (ICZN), all based on the Linnaean system of ranked taxa. (p. 107)

monophyletic_groups.label: Monophyletic Groups (Clades)
monophyletic_groups.summary: Groups consisting of an ancestor and all its descendants.
monophyletic_groups.details: Members of a monophyletic group share a more recent common ancestor with each other than with any organism outside the group. (p. 108)

polyphyletic_groups.label: Polyphyletic Groups
polyphyletic_groups.summary: Groups unified by characters not due to shared ancestry.
polyphyletic_groups.details: Groups recognized by collections of characters that do not reflect a single common evolutionary origin. (p. 108)

paraphyletic_groups.label: Paraphyletic Groups
paraphyletic_groups.summary: Groups that exclude certain descendants of a common ancestor.
paraphyletic_groups.details: Taxa that exclude descendants that have lost or transformed particular features (e.g., Reptilia excluding birds). (p. 108)

phylogenetic_definitions.label: Phylogenetic Definitions
phylogenetic_definitions.summary: Three primary methods for defining clades using speciﬁers (referent species/specimens).

phylocode.label: PhyloCode (ICPN)
phylocode.summary: The International Code of Phylogenetic Nomenclature.

regnum_database.label: RegNum
regnum_database.details: A required formal registration database for names and their associated phylogenetic definitions under the PhyloCode. (p. 109)

species_in_phylogenetics.label: Species in Phylogenetic Framework
species_in_phylogenetics.summary: The challenge of integrating rank-based species names into a rank-free phylogenetic system.

litu_concept.label: LITU
litu_concept.details: The smallest clades below which there is no phylogenetic structure, proposed as an alternative to the concept of 'species'. (p. 109)

praenomen_approach.label: Praenomen Approach
praenomen_approach.summary: PhyloCode's method for handling species binomens.
praenomen_approach.details: The first part of a species binomen (praenomen) is recommended to be a converted clade name, while the species name itself remains established under existing rank-based codes. (p. 110)

paleontology.label: Paleontology and the Fossil Record
paleontology.summary: The study of ancient life through the remains and traces preserved in sedimentary rocks.

taphonomy.label: Taphonomy
taphonomy.summary: The study of how organisms become preserved as fossils.

biostratinomy.label: Biostratinomy
biostratinomy.summary: Processes occurring between death and burial.
biostratinomy.details: Includes decay, scavenging, mechanical abrasion, chemical dissolution, and bioerosion. (p. 113)

permineralization.label: Permineralization
permineralization.details: Mineral-laden waters deposit precipitates in preexisting spaces in skeletal material (common in wood and bone). (p. 114)

petrifaction.label: Petrifaction
petrifaction.summary: Complete mineral replacement of organic matter.
petrifaction.details: The process in which organic matter is completely replaced by precipitating minerals. (p. 114)

replacement.label: Replacement
replacement.details: Both skeletal and soft tissue components are replaced by precipitating minerals. (p. 114)

lagerstatten.label: Lagerstätten
lagerstatten.details: Deposits that preserve soft tissues, often requiring anoxic conditions and rapid burial (e.g., Burgess Shale, Messel Oil Shale). (p. 114)

stratigraphy.label: Stratigraphy
stratigraphy.summary: The study of rock deposition patterns.

superposition_principle.label: Principle of Superposition
superposition_principle.details: Vertical successions of rock are ordered with the oldest strata at the bottom and the youngest at the top. (p. 112)

unconformity_fact.label: Unconformity
unconformity_fact.details: A surface separating two stratigraphic units that represents missing geologic time due to erosion or non-deposition. (p. 112)

time_averaging.label: Time Averaging
time_averaging.details: The mixing of individuals from different time intervals into a single sedimentary assemblage. (p. 112)

fossil_types.label: Types of Fossils
fossil_types.summary: Different forms of preserved biological evidence.

body_fossils.label: Body Fossils
body_fossils.details: Fossilized remains of a once-living organism, representing the actual body. (p. 112)

trace_fossils.label: Trace Fossils
trace_fossils.details: Records of behavior preserved in sediment, including footprints, burrows, feeding traces, and coprolites. (p. 112)

phanerozoic_diversity.label: Phanerozoic Marine Diversity
phanerozoic_diversity.summary: Diversity trends over the last 542 million years.

sepkoski_faunas.label: Sepkoski's Evolutionary Faunas
sepkoski_faunas.summary: Three statistically defined groups of marine organisms.

cambrian_fauna.label: Cambrian Fauna
cambrian_fauna.details: Dominated by trilobites and small grazers/deposit feeders. (p. 117)

paleozoic_fauna.label: Paleozoic Fauna
paleozoic_fauna.details: Characterized by brachiopods, crinoids, and certain corals/bryozoans feeding on suspended material. (p. 117)

modern_fauna.label: Modern Fauna
modern_fauna.details: Characterized by snails, clams (often infaunal), and a host of predators (crabs, fish, mammals). (p. 117)

paleodb.label: PaleoDB
paleodb.details: A global database of fossil occurrences used to create sampling-standardized diversity curves to correct for sampling bias. (p. 118)

origins_of_life.label: The Origin of Life
origins_of_life.summary: The prebiotic chemical processes that led to the first living systems.

protocell_concept.label: Protocell
protocell_concept.summary: An evolutionary precursor to the cell.
protocell_concept.details: A microscopic membrane-bounded system of interacting polymers that represents an evolutionary stage on the pathway to the origin of life. (p. 120)

prebiotic_sites.label: Plausible Sites for Origin of Life
prebiotic_sites.summary: Environmental settings that could drive prebiotic chemistry.

clay_surfaces.label: Clay Surfaces
clay_surfaces.details: Proposed by Bernal and Cairns-Smith; montmorillonite clay can adsorb nucleotides and facilitate polymerization. (p. 122)

iron_sulfur_world.label: Iron-Sulfur World
iron_sulfur_world.details: Proposed by Wächtershäuser; pyrite (iron sulfide) surface charges and reactions drive early metabolic pathways. (p. 122)

global_ice_sheet.label: Global Ice Sheet
global_ice_sheet.details: Proposed by Bada and Miller; organics preserved in ice are released during impact melting to initiate reactions. (p. 122)

liquid_water.label: Liquid Water
liquid_water.summary: The universal solvent for prebiotic chemistry.
liquid_water.details: Required as a dilute solution for potential monomers (amino acids, nucleobases, sugars). (p. 123)

energy_source.label: Energy Source
energy_source.details: Energy required to link monomers into random polymers. (p. 123)

amphiphiles.label: Amphiphiles
amphiphiles.details: Molecules having both hydrophilic and hydrophobic components (e.g., fatty acids), which self-assemble into lipid bilayers and vesicles. (p. 120)

wet_dry_cycles.label: Wet-Dry Cycles
wet_dry_cycles.details: Hydrothermal cycles that concentrate reactants during drying and encapsulate them in vesicles upon rewetting. (p. 124)

prokaryotic_evolution.label: Evolution in the Prokaryotic Grade
prokaryotic_evolution.summary: The evolution of cellular organisms lacking a nucleus, comprising Bacteria and Archaea.

prokaryote_definition.label: Prokaryote Definition
prokaryote_definition.summary: A grade of organization, not a monophyletic group.
prokaryote_definition.details: Defined by the absence of a double-membrane-bounded nucleus. Because this is an ancestral state, prokaryotes are paraphyletic. (p. 127)

bacteria_domain.label: Domain Bacteria
bacteria_domain.summary: One of the primary domains of life.

bacterial_characteristics.label: Bacterial Characteristics
bacterial_characteristics.details: Characterized by distinct rRNA sequences and cell walls containing peptidoglycan. (p. 128)

major_bacterial_phyla.label: Major Bacterial Phyla
major_bacterial_phyla.summary: Key groups within the Bacteria domain.

cyanobacteria_fact.label: Cyanobacteria
cyanobacteria_fact.details: Capable of oxygenic photosynthesis; ancestors of eukaryotic plastids. (p. 129)

proteobacteria_fact.label: Proteobacteria
proteobacteria_fact.summary: A diverse group divided into five classes.
proteobacteria_fact.details: Includes Alpha (rhizobia), Beta (nitrifiers), Gamma (E. coli), Delta (myxobacteria), and Epsilon (Helicobacter). (p. 129)

firmicutes_actinobacteria.label: Firmicutes and Actinobacteria
firmicutes_actinobacteria.details: Characterized by multiple peptidoglycan layers; includes Bacillus and Mycobacterium. (p. 129)

archaeal_characteristics.label: Archaeal Characteristics
archaeal_characteristics.details: Distinguished by ether-linked lipids in cell membranes and the absence of peptidoglycan in cell walls. (p. 128)

crenarchaeota.label: Crenarchaeota
crenarchaeota.details: Often sulfur-dependent hyperthermophiles; some are termed 'Eocytes' in theories regarding eukaryote origins. (p. 129)

transformation_fact.label: Transformation
transformation_fact.details: Uptake of free DNA from the environment and integration into the cell genome. (p. 128)

conjugation_fact.label: Conjugation
conjugation_fact.details: Process of DNA transfer between two cells joined by pili. (p. 128)

transduction_fact.label: Transduction
transduction_fact.details: The transfer of foreign DNA into a prokaryotic cell via a phage (virus). (p. 132)

eukaryote_definition.label: Eukaryote Definition
eukaryote_definition.details: Defined by the presence of a double-membrane-bound nucleus and a protein-based cytoskeleton. (p. 135)

endosymbiosis_mitochondria.label: Mitochondrial Endosymbiosis
endosymbiosis_mitochondria.details: Mitochondria were acquired through the endosymbiosis of an alphaproteobacterium. (p. 136)

eukaryotic_clades.label: Major Eukaryotic Clades
eukaryotic_clades.summary: The primary phylogenetic groupings of eukaryotes.

opisthokonta.label: Opisthokonta
opisthokonta.details: A major clade that includes both animals and fungi. (p. 139)

amoebozoa.label: Amoebozoa
amoebozoa.details: One of the four major eukaryotic clades. (p. 139)

excavata.label: Excavata
excavata.details: One of the four major eukaryotic clades. (p. 139)

sar_clade.label: SAR Clade
sar_clade.summary: Supergroup of Stramenopiles, Alveolates, and Rhizaria.
sar_clade.details: A major clade comprising Stramenopiles, Alveolates, and Rhizaria. (p. 139)

major_clades.label: Major Eukaryotic Clades
major_clades.summary: The primary monophyletic groups that organize eukaryotic diversity based on molecular and morphological data.

opistho_animals.label: Animals (Metazoa)
opistho_animals.summary: Multicellular eukaryotes; closest living relatives are choanoflagellates. Sponge cells called choanocytes share similar structures with choanoflagellates.

fact_opistho_animal_affinity.label: Animal-Choanoflagellate Affinity
fact_opistho_animal_affinity.summary: The affinity of animals with choanoflagellates was noted over a century ago due to the similarity between choanocytes and choanoflagellates (p. 139).

opistho_fungi.label: Fungi
opistho_fungi.summary: Heterotrophic eukaryotes with chitin cell walls and absorptive nutrition (p. 152).

opistho_others.label: Other Opisthokonts
opistho_others.summary: Includes Ichthyosporea (fish parasites) and the slime mold Fonticula (p. 139).

tubulinea.label: Tubulinea
tubulinea.summary: The largest clade within Amoebozoa, defined by the morphological synapomorphy of cylindrical pseudopodia with monoaxial streaming (p. 139).

fact_tubulinea_examples.label: Tubulinea Examples
fact_tubulinea_examples.summary: Includes Amoeba proteus and lobose testate (shelled) amoebae used in paleoclimate reconstruction (p. 139).

amoebozoa_examples.label: Amoebozoa Examples
amoebozoa_examples.summary: Includes Amoeba proteus, two clades of slime molds, and Entamoeba histolytica (agent of amoebic dysentery) (p. 139).

excavata_mitochondria.label: Excavata Mitochondrial Reduction
excavata_mitochondria.summary: Many members are anaerobic and possess highly reduced mitochondria termed hydrogenosomes or mitosomes (p. 139).

fact_long_branch_attraction.label: Long-Branch Attraction in Excavata
fact_long_branch_attraction.summary: Rapid evolution rates in some parasites artificially placed them at the base of early rDNA trees, leading to the disproven hypothesis that they branched off before mitochondria acquisition (p. 139).

excavata_parasites.label: Parasitic Excavates
excavata_parasites.summary: Includes Giardia (diarrhea), Trypanosomes (sleeping sickness), and Trichomonas vaginalis (trichomoniasis) (p. 139).

euglenids.label: Euglenids
euglenids.summary: A lineage of Excavata that acquired photosynthesis by engulfing a green alga endosymbiont (p. 139).

stramenopiles.label: Stramenopiles
stramenopiles.summary: Defined by the ultrastructural synapomorphy of specific hairs on one of their flagella (p. 139).

fact_stramenopile_examples.label: Stramenopile Examples
fact_stramenopile_examples.summary: Includes diatoms (silica shells), kelps, and Phytophthora (cause of Irish potato famine) (p. 139).

alveolates.label: Alveolates
alveolates.summary: Defined by ultrastructural sacs called alveoli underlying the cell membrane for rigidity (p. 139).

fact_alveolate_examples.label: Alveolate Examples
fact_alveolate_examples.summary: Includes ciliates, dinoflagellates (critical for coral reefs), and apicomplexa (malaria parasite) (p. 139).

rhizaria.label: Rhizaria
rhizaria.summary: A heterogeneous collection of amoebae, flagellates, and parasites lacking diagnostic ultrastructural features; characterized by filose or reticulating pseudopodia (p. 139).

photosynthesis_distribution.label: Distribution of Photosynthesis
photosynthesis_distribution.summary: Photosynthesis is patchily distributed across eukaryotes via endosymbiosis.

primary_endosymbiosis.label: Primary Endosymbiosis
primary_endosymbiosis.summary: The engulfment of a single cyanobacterium over a billion years ago, leading to plastids with small circular genomes (p. 140).

primary_lineages.label: Primary Photosynthetic Lineages
primary_lineages.summary: Includes green algae, red algae, and glaucophytes; hypothesis suggests they form a monophyletic clade (p. 139).

secondary_endosymbiosis.label: Secondary Endosymbiosis
secondary_endosymbiosis.summary: The engulfment of a unicellular red or green alga by a nonphotosynthetic eukaryote (p. 140).

secondary_remnants.label: Secondary Endosymbiosis Remnants
secondary_remnants.summary: Cryptomonads (red algal remnant nucleus) and chlorarachniophytes (green algal remnant nucleus) (p. 140).

paulinella_endosymbiosis.label: Paulinella Endosymbiosis
paulinella_endosymbiosis.summary: A second independent primary endosymbiosis of a cyanobacterium by the amoeba Paulinella within Rhizaria, occurring ~65 Ma (p. 140).

kleptoplasty.label: Kleptoplasty
kleptoplasty.summary: The retention of 'stolen' plastids from food organisms, as seen in the sea slug Elysia (p. 140).

genome_diversity.label: Genome Diversity in Microbial Eukaryotes
genome_diversity.summary: Variations in genome content through ploidy-level shifts and differential amplification (p. 141).

germ_somatic_segregation.label: Germ Line and Somatic Genome Segregation
germ_somatic_segregation.summary: Separation of inherited genomes from somatic genomes that accumulate variation.

segregation_animals.label: Animal Genome Segregation
segregation_animals.summary: Germ line cells are sequestered early; in copepods, nematodes, and hagfish, somatic genomes are extensively modified via chromosome fragmentation (p. 142).

segregation_ciliates.label: Ciliate Genome Segregation
segregation_ciliates.summary: Contain a micronucleus (germ line, few long chromosomes) and a macronucleus (somatic, fragmented into hundreds/thousands of tiny chromosomes) (p. 142).

segregation_foraminifera.label: Foraminifera Genome Segregation
segregation_foraminifera.summary: One nucleus in the multinucleate life cycle expands and becomes transcriptionally active, while generative nuclei remain quiescent (p. 142).

multicellularity_origins.label: Origins of Multicellularity
multicellularity_origins.summary: Multicellularity evolved many times independently across eukaryotic lineages.

multicellular_algae.label: Multicellular Algae
multicellular_algae.summary: Includes giant kelps, red algae, and several origins within green algae (p. 142).

slime_mold_multicellularity.label: Slime Mold Multicellularity
slime_mold_multicellularity.summary: Evolution of multicellular fruiting bodies for dispersal, including dictyostelids and acrasids (p. 142).

plant_phylogeny.label: Plant Phylogenetic Framework
plant_phylogeny.summary: Plants are a monophyletic group defined by chlorophylls a and b, and starch storage in plastids (p. 143).

streptophytes.label: Streptophytes
streptophytes.summary: Clade including land plants and charophycean green algae (Coleochaetae, Chara) (p. 143).

plant_clades.label: Plant Groups
plant_clades.summary: Major groupings including Tracheophytes (vascular), Spermatophytes (seed), and Angiosperms (flowering) (p. 143).

fact_paraphyletic_plants.label: Paraphyletic Plant Groups
fact_paraphyletic_plants.summary: Includes 'green algae' (non-land plants), 'bryophytes' (non-vascular land plants), 'pteridophytes' (non-seed vascular plants), and 'gymnosperms' (non-flowering seed plants) (p. 143).

archegonium.label: Archegonium
archegonium.summary: Flask-like structure where eggs are formed and fertilized, and embryos begin development (p. 144).

sporopollenin.label: Sporopollenin
sporopollenin.summary: Complex biopolymer impregnating spore walls to resist desiccation (p. 144).

cuticle_stomata.label: Cuticle and Stomata
cuticle_stomata.summary: Waxy cuticle prevents water loss; stomata are pores for gas/water exchange (except in liverworts) (p. 144).

vascular_plant_evolution.label: Vascular Plant (Tracheophyte) Evolution
vascular_plant_evolution.summary: Characterized by specialized vascular tissues and larger sporophytes.

vascular_tissues.label: Vascular Tissues
vascular_tissues.summary: Xylem (water-conducting, contains tracheids/vessels, lignified walls) and Phloem (sugar/nutrient conducting, contains sieve cells) (p. 143).

lycophytes.label: Lycophytes
lycophytes.summary: Early vascular branch distinguished by kidney-shaped sporangia; includes zosterophylls (extinct) and lycopods (p. 145).

euphyllophytes.label: Euphyllophytes
euphyllophytes.summary: Second major vascular lineage giving rise to ferns, horsetails, and seed plants (p. 146).

lignophytes.label: Lignophytes
lignophytes.summary: Defined by a bifacial cambium allowing for secondary xylem (wood) and secondary phloem production (p. 146).

progymnosperms.label: Progymnosperms
progymnosperms.summary: Free-sporing plants (e.g., Archaeopteris) with a bifacial cambium, intermediate to seed plants (p. 146).

seed_plant_evolution.label: Seed Plant (Spermatophyte) Evolution
seed_plant_evolution.summary: Innovation of ovules and pollination, reducing dependence on water for fertilization (p. 147).

ovule_definition.label: Ovule
ovule_definition.summary: A megasporangium enveloped by an integument that contains a seed after fertilization (p. 143).

pollination.label: Pollination
pollination.summary: Transport of small male gametophytes (pollen) to ovules via wind, water, or animals (p. 147).

angiosperm_evolution.label: Angiosperm (Flowering Plant) Evolution
angiosperm_evolution.summary: The most diverse terrestrial plant group, characterized by flowers, carpels, and double fertilization.

angiosperm_traits.label: Angiosperm Vegetative/Reproductive Traits
angiosperm_traits.summary: Reticulate leaf veins, xylem vessels, ovules enclosed in carpels, and pollination via stigma (p. 147).

double_fertilization.label: Double Fertilization
double_fertilization.summary: One male gamete fuses with the egg; another fuses with a diploid nucleus to form triploid endosperm nutritive tissue (p. 148).

fungal_evolution.label: Evolution of Fungi
fungal_evolution.summary: Clade in the Unikonta supergroup; characterized by chitin cell walls and absorptive heterotrophy (p. 152).

basal_fungal_lineages.label: Basal Fungal Lineages
basal_fungal_lineages.summary: Paraphyletic assemblage including chytrids and zygomycetes.

chytrids.label: Chytrids
chytrids.summary: Fungi that produce swimming zoospores; include Chytridiomycota, Neocallimastigomycota, Blastocladiomycota, and Rozellida/Cryptomycota (p. 153).

zygomycetes.label: Zygomycetes
zygomycetes.summary: Non-flagellated fungi with mycelia lacking regular septa; includes Mucoromycotina, Glomeromycota, etc. (p. 153).

arbuscular_mycorrhizae.label: Arbuscular-Mycorrhizal (AM) Associations
arbuscular_mycorrhizae.summary: Symbioses of Glomeromycota occurring in ~80% of plant species, facilitating land colonization (p. 154).

dikarya.label: Dikarya
dikarya.summary: Clade defined by the dikaryon: a stable binucleate condition formed by cytoplasmic fusion of monokaryons without immediate nuclear fusion (p. 155).

ascomycota.label: Ascomycota
ascomycota.summary: Produce spores internally within a sac-like ascus (p. 155).

basidiomycota.label: Basidiomycota
basidiomycota.summary: Produce spores externally on a pedestal-shaped basidium; often have clamp connections for nuclear apportionment (p. 155).

dikarya_innovations.label: Dikarya Ecological Innovations
dikarya_innovations.summary: Development of complex fruiting bodies and specialized nutritional modes.

wood_decay.label: Wood Decay
wood_decay.summary: White rot (degrades carbohydrate and lignin via class II fungal peroxidases) and Brown rot (chemically modifies but does not degrade lignin) (p. 156).

fungal_mutualism.label: Fungal Mutualisms
fungal_mutualism.summary: Ectomycorrhizae (ECM) - hyphae ensheathe roots; Lichens - association with algae/cyanobacteria; Endophytes - cryptic fungi in plants (p. 157).

animal_evolution.label: Evolution of Animals (Metazoa)
animal_evolution.summary: Multicellular organisms undergoing gastrulation; diversification peaked during the Cambrian Explosion (543-510 Ma).

animal_phylogeny.label: Animal Phylogenetic Framework
animal_phylogeny.summary: Animals diverge from choanoflagellates. Major clades include Porifera, Cnidaria, and Bilateria.

porifera.label: Porifera (Sponges)
porifera.summary: Benthic filter feeders with choanocytes; lack true tissues, muscles, or nerves (p. 161).

cnidaria.label: Cnidaria
cnidaria.summary: Radially symmetrical, diploblastic animals with nematocysts (stinging cells) and a diffuse nerve net (p. 161).

bilateria.label: Bilateria
bilateria.summary: Triploblastic animals with bilateral symmetry and a mesoderm, divided into Protostomia and Deuterostomia (p. 161).

protostomes.label: Protostomia
protostomes.summary: Blastopore generally becomes the mouth. Includes Lophotrochozoa and Ecdysozoa (p. 161).

deuterostomes.label: Deuterostomia
deuterostomes.summary: Blastopore generally becomes the anus; coelom develops via enterocoely (p. 161).

animal_innovations.label: Key Animal Innovations
animal_innovations.summary: Molecular and structural transitions during the origin of Metazoa.

cell_adhesion_communication.label: Cell Adhesion and Communication
cell_adhesion_communication.summary: Use of C-type lectins, cadherins, and protein kinase signaling pathways; present in choanoflagellates before animals (p. 163).

gastrulation.label: Gastrulation
gastrulation.summary: Reorganization of cells into layers, critical for spatial organization and differentiation of cell types (p. 163).

nervous_system_origin.label: Origin of the Nervous System
nervous_system_origin.summary: Progression from protoneuronal components in sponges to diffuse nerve nets in cnidarians, then centralized systems in bilaterians (p. 164).

arthropod_evolution.label: Evolution of Arthropods
arthropod_evolution.summary: The most successful animal clade, members of Ecdysozoa characterized by a segmented body plan and chitinous exoskeleton.

arthropod_traits.label: Arthropod Anatomical Traits
arthropod_traits.summary: Segmented bodies, jointed legs, and a sclerotized exoskeleton (tanned via sclerotization) that is molted (p. 167).

tagmosis.label: Tagmosis
tagmosis.summary: The specialization of body regions (tagma) regulated by Hox genes (e.g., head-thorax-abdomen) (p. 167).

chelicerata.label: Chelicerata
chelicerata.summary: Sister group to other arthropods; identified by chelicerae (mouth appendages). Includes arachnids and horseshoe crabs (p. 168).

myriapoda.label: Myriapoda
myriapoda.summary: Terrestrial group including millipedes and centipedes; part of Mandibulata (p. 169).

pancrustacea.label: Pancrustacea
pancrustacea.summary: Clade combining crustaceans and hexapods (insects), demonstrating that insects are a crustacean lineage (p. 170).

insecta.label: Insecta
insecta.summary: The most species-rich arthropod group; innovations include flight and complete metamorphosis (Holometabola) (p. 170).

insect_evolution.label: Insect Evolution
insect_evolution.summary: The evolutionary development of insects, focusing on flight, metamorphosis, and life history specializations.

insect_flight.label: Origin and Evolution of Insect Flight
insect_flight.summary: The transition of insects to aerial locomotion and the subsequent modification of wings.

flight_origin_theories.label: Theories on Wing Origin
flight_origin_theories.summary: Hypotheses regarding the ancestral structures that became wings.

theory_thoracic_lobes.label: Modified Thoracic Lobes
theory_thoracic_lobes.summary: Wings originated from thoracic lobes once used for gliding.

theory_gills.label: Gill Derivative Theory
theory_gills.summary: Wings developed from gills, similar to those found on mayfly nymphs' abdomens.

theory_locomotory.label: Locomotory Paddles Theory
theory_locomotory.summary: Pre-flight wings served as paddles for skimming water surfaces.

theory_spiracle_covers.label: Spiracle Covers Theory
theory_spiracle_covers.summary: Pre-flight wings served as covers for spiracles.

theory_thermoregulation.label: Thermoregulator Theory
theory_thermoregulation.summary: Pre-flight wings served as tools for temperature regulation.

theory_sexual_selection.label: Sexual Selection Theory
theory_sexual_selection.summary: Pre-flight wings played a role in sexual selection displays.

flight_evidence.label: Evidence for Flight Evolution
flight_evidence.summary: Behavioral and ecological evidence supporting the transition to powered flight.

dudley_studies.label: Dudley et al. Research
dudley_studies.summary: Studies on jumping and gliding in terrestrial insects (e.g., Thysanura/bristletails) provide evidence for flight originating from jumping -> directed gliding -> powered flight.

devonian_vegetation.label: Devonian Environmental Context
devonian_vegetation.summary: The origin of flight corresponds with the Devonian period when vegetation became taller and more tree/shrub-like.

wing_modifications.label: Wing Modifications
wing_modifications.summary: Evolutionary changes to wings for alternate purposes.

elytra_beetles.label: Elytra
elytra_beetles.summary: Hardened forewings in beetles that function as protective covers.

halteres_flies.label: Halteres
halteres_flies.summary: Greatly reduced hindwings in flies that function as gyroscopes.

wing_loss.label: Secondary Wing Loss
wing_loss.summary: The repeated evolutionary loss of wings across various lineages.

order_wide_loss.label: Order-wide Wing Loss
order_wide_loss.summary: Wing loss exhibited by every species in an order, such as fleas and lice.

lineage_specific_loss.label: Lineage-specific Wing Loss
lineage_specific_loss.summary: Loss of wings in individual lineages, e.g., sheep keds and bat flies (ectoparasitic lifestyles).

complete_metamorphosis.label: Complete Metamorphosis
complete_metamorphosis.summary: The evolutionary innovation of three distinct life stages, enabling massive diversification.

holometabola.label: Holometabola
holometabola.summary: Insects undergoing complete metamorphosis; includes beetles, moths, wasps (bees/ants), and flies. The most diverse arthropod lineage.

selective_advantages.label: Advantages of Complete Metamorphosis
selective_advantages.summary: Biological benefits that drove the success of Holometabola.

competition_avoidance.label: Avoidance of Competition
competition_avoidance.summary: Larvae and adults often occupy different habitats and use different diets, avoiding direct competition.

internal_wing_development.label: Internal Wing Development
internal_wing_development.summary: Allows larvae to feed within substrates (wood, plant matter, other organisms) unsuitable for adults.

lifecycle_brevity.label: Brevity of Life Cycle
lifecycle_brevity.summary: Reduces the risk of predation for wingless larval stages by shortening the duration of that stage.

developmental_control.label: Control Over Development
developmental_control.summary: The ability of holometabolous lineages to finely tune larval development.

cyclorraphan_puparium.label: Cyclorraphan Puparium
cyclorraphan_puparium.summary: Modified metamorphosis where the pupa is encased in an impervious puparium made from the last larval skin, allowing development in toxic or low-oxygen substrates.

life_history_specializations.label: Life History Specializations
life_history_specializations.summary: Diverse adaptations in feeding, communication, and social organization among arthropods.

feeding_strategies.label: Arthropod Feeding Strategies
feeding_strategies.summary: Diverse dietary niches including nectar/pollen feeders, decomposers, predators, plant feeders, blood feeders, and parasites.

spider_silk.label: Silk Usage in Araneomorphae
spider_silk.summary: Coordination of morphological and behavioral adaptations for prey capture and shelter construction since the Devonian (340 Ma).

eusociality.label: Eusociality
eusociality.summary: Group living with division of labor, emerging independently in termites, ants, paper wasps, and honey bees.

tetrapod_evolution.label: Tetrapod Evolution
tetrapod_evolution.summary: The transition of vertebrates from finned fishes to limbed terrestrial animals over 375 million years.

tetrapod_ancestry.label: Tetrapod Ancestry
tetrapod_ancestry.summary: The phylogenetic path from bony fishes to early tetrapods.

osteichthyes.label: Osteichthyes (Bony Fishes)
osteichthyes.summary: First appear in the Silurian (439-408 Ma); diverged into ray-finned and fleshy-finned fishes.

sarcopterygii.label: Sarcopterygii (Fleshy-finned Fishes)
sarcopterygii.summary: Characterized by muscles and a robust skeleton within the fin; lepidotrichia are confined to margins.

crossopterygians.label: Crossopterygians
crossopterygians.summary: A group of Sarcopterygians; tetrapods specifically arose from the elpistostegalid group.

fish_tetrapod_transition.label: The Fish-Tetrapod Transition
fish_tetrapod_transition.summary: The anatomical changes enabling the move from water to land during the Late Devonian.

tiktaalik_roseae.label: Tiktaalik roseae
tiktaalik_roseae.summary: An amphibious transitional elpistostegalian (375 Ma) featuring eyes above the skull roof, a mobile neck (loss of operculo-gular bones), and wrist bones (ulnare, intermedium) supporting body weight on land.

early_tetrapods.label: Early Tetrapods
early_tetrapods.summary: Primitive tetrapods like Ichthyostega and Acanthostega that retained gills and finned tails but developed robust vertebral columns and polydactylous limbs.

amniote_origins.label: Amniote Origins
amniote_origins.summary: The evolution of the amniotic egg, allowing reproduction away from aqueous environments.

amniotic_egg_structure.label: The Amniotic Egg
amniotic_egg_structure.summary: Includes an eggshell membrane, amnion (watery environment), yolk sac (nutrition), allantois (waste), and chorioallantoic membrane (respiration).

amniote_skull_patterns.label: Amniote Skull Patterns
amniote_skull_patterns.summary: Classification of amniotes based on temporal fenestrae (openings for jaw muscles).

anapsid_skull.label: Anapsid
anapsid_skull.summary: Skulls where the muscle chamber is completely enclosed with no external fenestrae.

synapsid_skull.label: Synapsid
synapsid_skull.summary: Skulls possessing a single lateral temporal fenestra.

diapsid_skull.label: Diapsid
diapsid_skull.summary: Skulls possessing two temporal fenestrae, one above the other.

synapsid_lineage.label: Synapsid Evolution
synapsid_lineage.summary: The lineage leading to mammals, characterized by a transition through pelycosaurs and therapsids.

pelycosaurs.label: Pelycosaurs
pelycosaurs.summary: Early synapsids of the Late Pennsylvanian/Early Permian; some had dorsal sails for thermoregulation.

therapsids.label: Therapsids
therapsids.summary: Mammal-like reptiles that supplanted pelycosaurs; included Dinocephalia and Cynodonts (the most advanced, ancestral to mammals).

mammalian_innovations.label: Mammalian Anatomical Transitions
mammalian_innovations.summary: Specific skeletal changes tracing back to cynodonts.

jaw_joint_evolution.label: Jaw Joint Evolution
jaw_joint_evolution.summary: Shift from a quadrate-articular joint to a dentary-squamosal joint.

middle_ear_evolution.label: Middle Ear Evolution
middle_ear_evolution.summary: The articular and quadrate bones were retained and repurposed as the malleus and incus, joining the stapes.

dental_differentiation.label: Dental Differentiation
dental_differentiation.summary: Transition from homogeneous teeth to differentiated incisors, canines, premolars, and molars with tooth-on-tooth occlusion.

diapsid_lineage.label: Diapsid Evolution
diapsid_lineage.summary: The lineage including lepidosaurs and archosaurs.

lepidosaurs.label: Lepidosaurs
lepidosaurs.summary: Includes tuataras (Rhynchocephalia), lizards, and snakes. Characterized by epidermal shedding and caudal autotomy.

snake_evolution.label: Evolution of Snakes
snake_evolution.summary: Derived from lizards (possibly monitors or alligator lizards); feature right-aortic arch predominance and highly flexible cranial articulations.

aquatic_lepidosaurs.label: Aquatic Diapsids
aquatic_lepidosaurs.summary: Includes Mosasaurs, Plesiosaurs (sub-aqueous flight), and Ichthyosaurs (thunniform body, massive eyes for deep diving).

archosaurs.label: Archosaurs
archosaurs.summary: Diapsids dominating the Mesozoic, including crocodilians, pterosaurs, and dinosaurs.

archosaur_anatomy.label: Archosaur Anatomy
archosaur_anatomy.summary: Distinguished by an ant-orbital fenestra and a mandibular fenestra; includes thecodont (socket-implanted) teeth.

crocodilians.label: Crocodilian Evolution
crocodilians.summary: Evolved a secondary bony palate with internal choanae migrating posteriorly, separating nasal and oropharyngeal passages for semi-aquatic ambush predation.

pterosaurs.label: Pterosaurs
pterosaurs.summary: First powered fliers; wing membrane (brachiopatagium) extended to a hyperelongated fourth digit; possessed furry pelage (endothermy).

dinosaurs.label: Dinosaur Evolution
dinosaurs.summary: Divided by pelvic structure into Ornithischia (bird hip, herbivorous) and Saurischia (lizard hip, includes sauropods and theropods).

ornithischians.label: Ornithischians
ornithischians.summary: Herbivores with predentary bones and keratinous beaks; developed diverse defenses (armor, spikes, horns).

saurischians.label: Saurischians
saurischians.summary: Includes Sauropodomorphs (long necks, graviportal limbs) and Theropods (carnivorous, bipedal).

avian_origins.label: Origins of Avian Flight
avian_origins.summary: Feathers evolved for thermoregulation. Flight theories include the 'cursorial' (ground-up) and 'arboreal' (trees-down) scenarios, which are likely not mutually exclusive.

hominin_origins.label: Origin of Hominins
hominin_origins.summary: Divergence from chimpanzee/bonobo lineage 5-7 Ma; initial transition to bipedalism.

early_candidates.label: Early Hominin Candidates
early_candidates.summary: Includes Sahelanthropus tchadensis (7 Ma), Orrorin tugenensis (6 Ma), and Ardipithecus (4.4-5.5 Ma).

bipedal_adaptations.label: Bipedalism
bipedal_adaptations.summary: Orthograde posture; involves pelvic changes (bowl-shaped) and foot adaptations (aligned first toe, arches).

australopithecines.label: Australopithecines
australopithecines.summary: Obligate bipeds (e.g., A. afarensis, A. africanus) with small brains (~450 ml) and some climbing abilities. Includes robust forms (A. boisei) specialized for hard seeds/leaves.

genus_homo.label: Genus Homo
genus_homo.summary: Emergence ~1.8 Ma characterized by larger brains, higher quality diets (meat), and tool use.

homo_erectus.label: Homo erectus
homo_erectus.summary: First hominin to disperse widely into Eurasia; brain size 600-900 ml; used Acheulean tools.

homo_habilis.label: Homo habilis
homo_habilis.summary: Early Homo species (1.9-1.5 Ma) with brains 500-750 ml.

cognitive_evolution.label: Cognitive and Social Evolution
cognitive_evolution.summary: Brain expansion driven by metabolic needs (meat diet) and social complexity (food sharing, egalitarian cooperation).

stone_tool_industries.label: Stone Tool Evolution
stone_tool_industries.summary: Transition from Oldowan (basic flakes/cores) to Acheulean (symmetrical hand axes) to Middle Stone Age (prepared core technique, hafted points).

recent_human_evolution.label: Recent Human Evolution
recent_human_evolution.summary: Evolution of modern humans (H. sapiens), regional mixtures, and adaptations to culture/environment.

neanderthals_denisovans.label: Neanderthals and Denisovans
neanderthals_denisovans.summary: Regional archaic humans; Neanderthals evolved traits for cold environments (barrel chests, robust bones). Modern non-Africans carry 2-4% Neanderthal DNA; Melanesians carry Denisovan DNA.

agricultural_revolution.label: Impact of Agriculture
agricultural_revolution.summary: Shift to sedentary life led to more gracile skeletons, smaller teeth/jaws (lack of wisdom teeth), and increased exposure to pathogens.

recent_selective_pressures.label: Recent Selective Pressures
recent_selective_pressures.summary: includes malaria resistance alleles, lactose tolerance, high-altitude oxygen transport, and pigmentation changes based on latitude.

selection_mechanism.label: Mechanism of Natural Selection
selection_mechanism.summary: A non-random process of sorting by reproductive success based on phenotypic differences.

conditions_for_selection.label: Necessary Conditions for Natural Selection
conditions_for_selection.summary: Four conditions: Variation in reproductive success, variation in the trait, non-zero correlation between trait and success, and heritability of the trait.

genetic_drift_vs_selection.label: Genetic Drift vs Natural Selection
genetic_drift_vs_selection.summary: Genetic drift is the random component of variation in reproductive success (sampling error); natural selection is the non-random component.

fitness_and_units.label: Fitness and Units of Selection
fitness_and_units.summary: Measures of reproductive performance and the entities they apply to.

replicators_vs_interactors.label: Replicators and Interactors
replicators_vs_interactors.summary: The replicator is the information copier (DNA/gene); the interactor is the organism in its ecological role. Selection acts through interactors to change replicator frequencies.

pleiotropy_epistasis.label: Pleiotropy and Epistasis
pleiotropy_epistasis.summary: Pleiotropy: one gene affects multiple traits. Epistasis: one trait is influenced by multiple genes.

trade_offs.label: Evolutionary Trade-offs
trade_offs.summary: An evolutionary change that increases fitness in one trait or context but causes a decrease in another.

frequency_dependence.label: Frequency-Dependent Selection
frequency_dependence.summary: Fitness of a phenotype depends on its frequency; negative frequency dependence (advantage of being rare) maintains population variation.

levels_of_selection.label: Levels and Units of Selection
levels_of_selection.summary: The biological hierarchy at which selection operates.

individual_selection.label: Individual Selection
individual_selection.summary: Selection among individual organisms within populations; the primary driver of adaptive features.

adaptation_concepts.label: Adaptation Concepts
adaptation_concepts.summary: The study of features evolved via natural selection.

adaptation_process_state.label: Adaptation as Process and State
adaptation_process_state.summary: As a process: the portion of evolutionary change driven by selection. As a state: the aspect of a trait reliably ascribed to past selection.

adaptationist_storytelling.label: Adaptationist Storytelling
adaptationist_storytelling.summary: The critique that biologists may over-attribute traits to selection without excluding genetic drift or structural constraints.

major_transitions.label: Major Evolutionary Transitions
major_transitions.summary: Transitions in individuality where free-living biological entities integrate into a cohesive whole, increasing hierarchical complexity (p. 204).

transition_examples.label: Examples of Evolutionary Transitions
transition_examples.summary: Specific historical shifts in biological organization (p. 204).

ex_rep_net.label: Replicators to Networks
ex_rep_net.summary: Transition from individual replicators to networks of replicators (p. 204).

ex_gene_chrom.label: Genes to Chromosomes
ex_gene_chrom.summary: Transition from individual genes to integrated chromosomes (p. 204).

ex_pro_euk.label: Prokaryotic to Eukaryotic
ex_pro_euk.summary: Transition from prokaryotic cells to eukaryotic cells containing organelles (p. 204).

ex_single_multi.label: Single-celled to Multicellular
ex_single_multi.summary: Transition from single-celled organisms to multicelled organisms (p. 204).

ex_solitary_colony.label: Solitary to Integrated Colonies
ex_solitary_colony.summary: Transition from solitary organisms to integrated colonies (p. 204).

transition_mechanisms.label: Mechanisms of Transition
transition_mechanisms.summary: The biological and selection-based requirements for successful evolutionary transitions (p. 204-205).

multilevel_selection_trans.label: Multilevel Selection in Transitions
multilevel_selection_trans.summary: During transitions, selection can act at multiple hierarchical levels (e.g., between cells and between cell groups); higher-level selection must dominate for the group to emerge as an 'evolutionary individual' (p. 204).

conflict_suppression.label: Conflict Suppression and Policing
conflict_suppression.summary: Mechanisms required to prevent 'cheaters' (selfish lower-level units) from undermining the integrity of the whole, aligning reproductive interests of units with the corporate body (p. 204).

individuality_concept.label: Individuality as a Derived Trait
individuality_concept.summary: Individuality is not a given but a derived trait resulting from the union of cooperative units (e.g., eukaryotic cells as multispecies assemblages), necessitating explanation via multilevel selection (p. 205).

pop_selection_theory.label: Theory of Selection in Populations
pop_selection_theory.summary: The study of how natural selection influences allele and genotype frequencies within populations (p. 205-214).

abs_viability.label: Absolute Viability
abs_viability.summary: The probability of survival from zygote to adult (p. 206).

bateman_principle.label: Bateman's Principle
bateman_principle.summary: Females generally invest more in offspring and remate less quickly than males, leading to greater variation in male reproductive success (p. 206).

cline_def.label: Cline
cline_def.summary: A gradual change in allele frequency along a geographical transect (p. 206).

fitness_def.label: Fitness
fitness_def.summary: The probability of survival from zygote to adult, or more generally, the performance of a genotype in survival and reproduction (p. 206).

fixation_def.label: Fixation
fixation_def.summary: When an allele is the only one present in a population, making it monomorphic (p. 206).

mean_fitness_def.label: Mean Fitness (w)
mean_fitness_def.summary: The average probability of survival from zygote to adult in a population, calculated as the sum of genotype frequency times genotype viability (p. 206).

selection_coeff.label: Selection Coefficient (s)
selection_coeff.summary: The difference in relative fitness between a particular genotype and the genotype with a relative fitness of 1 (p. 206).

dir_selection.label: Directional Selection
dir_selection.summary: Occurs when one homozygote has the highest fitness and the other the lowest; leads to the fixation of the most fit allele and monomorphism (p. 208).

dis_selection.label: Disruptive Selection
dis_selection.summary: Occurs when heterozygotes have lower fitness than either homozygote; leads to monomorphism for one of the alleles depending on initial frequency (p. 209).

stab_selection.label: Stabilizing Selection
stab_selection.summary: Occurs when heterozygotes have higher fitness than either homozygote (overdominance); preserves genetic variation and leads to a stable polymorphic equilibrium (p. 209).

selection_components.label: Components of Selection
selection_components.summary: The different life stages and mechanisms through which selection operates (p. 210-211).

viability_sel.label: Viability Selection
viability_sel.summary: Natural selection associated with differences in the probability of survival (p. 206).

fertility_sel.label: Fertility Selection
fertility_sel.summary: Natural selection associated with differences in the number of offspring produced, which may depend on the genotypes of both parents (p. 210).

sexual_sel.label: Sexual Selection
sexual_sel.summary: Selection based on probability of mating; includes male-male competition and female choice. Often conflicts with viability selection (p. 211).

gametic_sel.label: Gametic Selection
gametic_sel.summary: Differences in the probability of gametes accomplishing fertilization (e.g., sperm competition or pollen tube growth) (p. 211).

polymorphism_maintenance.label: Maintenance of Polymorphism
polymorphism_maintenance.summary: Mechanisms that prevent the fixation of a single allele, preserving genetic diversity (p. 211-212).

freq_dep_sel.label: Frequency-Dependent Selection
freq_dep_sel.summary: Fitness of a genotype depends on its frequency. Negative frequency dependence (rare types are more fit) maintains high diversity (p. 211).

spatial_var.label: Spatial Variation
spatial_var.summary: Different genotypes are favored in different habitats. Polymorphism is maintained if dispersal between habitats is limited or specific conditions are met (p. 211).

temporal_var.label: Temporal Variation
temporal_var.summary: Fitness of genotypes varies over time due to environmental changes unrelated to genotype frequency (p. 212).

pop_interactions.label: Selection and Other Evolutionary Processes
pop_interactions.summary: How selection interacts with mutation, migration, and drift (p. 212-213).

mut_sel_balance.label: Mutation-Selection Balance
mut_sel_balance.summary: An equilibrium where the loss of a deleterious allele via selection is balanced by its gain via mutation. Recessive alleles persist at higher frequencies than partially recessive ones (p. 212).

gene_flow_migration.label: Gene Flow and Migration
gene_flow_migration.summary: Movement of organisms between populations. Creates clines (gradual allele frequency changes along a transect) as a balance between local selection and gene flow (p. 212).

genetic_drift_inter.label: Genetic Drift Interaction
genetic_drift_inter.summary: Random changes in allele frequency. Selection predominates when Ne * s > 1; genetic drift predominates when Ne * s < 1 (p. 213).

inclusive_fitness_concept.label: Inclusive Fitness
inclusive_fitness_concept.summary: The sum of an individual's fitness effects on itself and others, each multiplied by the relatedness (r) to that party (p. 216).

hamiltons_rule.label: Hamilton's Rule
hamiltons_rule.summary: A trait is favored if -c + rb > 0, where c is cost to self, b is benefit to partner, and r is relatedness (p. 216).

social_selection_types.label: Kinds of Social Selection
social_selection_types.summary: Classification of interactions based on fitness effects on self and partner (p. 216).

altruism_def.label: Altruism
altruism_def.summary: Behavior costly to the performer but beneficial to others (p. 215).

mutual_benefit.label: Mutual Benefit
mutual_benefit.summary: Positive fitness effects on both the actor and the partner (p. 216).

selfish_behavior.label: Selfish Behavior
selfish_behavior.summary: Positive effect on self and negative effect on the partner (p. 216).

spite_def.label: Spite
spite_def.summary: Harm to both self and others; generally does not evolve unless it benefits other partners (e.g., bacteriocins) (p. 216).

haplodiploid_hyp.label: Haplodiploid Hypothesis
haplodiploid_hyp.summary: In Hymenoptera, females are diploid and males haploid. Full sisters share 75% of genes, which was hypothesized to drive the evolution of eusociality (p. 217).

kin_recognition.label: Kin Recognition Mechanisms
kin_recognition.summary: How organisms identify relatives to target behavior (p. 218).

proximity_recognition.label: Proximity Recognition
proximity_recognition.summary: Assuming neighbors or nest-mates are kin (p. 218).

phenotype_matching.label: Phenotype Matching
phenotype_matching.summary: Comparing unknown individuals to a learned or innate template of characteristic cues (p. 218).

croziers_paradox.label: Crozier's Paradox
croziers_paradox.summary: The puzzle of how variability is maintained at cue loci when the most common cue allele should theoretically be favored (p. 218).

phenotypic_selection.label: Phenotypic Selection on Quantitative Traits
phenotypic_selection.summary: The study of selection on continuous traits and the resulting evolutionary responses (p. 221-229).

selection_requisites.label: Three Requisites for Selection
selection_requisites.summary: Necessary conditions for selection to cause evolutionary change (p. 222).

req_variation.label: Variation
req_variation.summary: Differences among individuals (quantitative or qualitative) as the essential substrate (p. 222).

req_heritability.label: Heritability
req_heritability.summary: Offspring must resemble parents for effects to persist across generations (p. 222).

req_diff_reproduction.label: Differential Reproduction
req_diff_reproduction.summary: Some individuals must be more successful than others in leaving copies of themselves (p. 222).

statistical_framework.label: Statistical Framework of Selection
statistical_framework.summary: Measuring selection using covariance and the Price Equation (p. 223).

price_equation.label: Price Equation
price_equation.summary: Change in average trait (Delta z) is predicted by the covariance between fitness (w) and the trait (z): Delta z = Cov(w, z) / mean(w) (p. 223).

selection_differential_s.label: Phenotypic Selection Differential (s)
selection_differential_s.summary: A metric for the strength of total selection on a trait based on the covariance of fitness and phenotype (p. 223).

genetic_response_quant.label: Genetic Response to Selection
genetic_response_quant.summary: How phenotypic selection is translated into evolutionary change (p. 224).

breeders_equation.label: Breeder's Equation
breeders_equation.summary: Response to selection (R) is the product of heritability (h^2) and the selection differential (s): R = h^2 * s (p. 224).

quant_selection_modes.label: Modes of Quantitative Selection
quant_selection_modes.summary: Statistical forms of selection based on fitness functions (p. 225-226).

q_dir_sel.label: Quantitative Directional Selection
q_dir_sel.summary: Changes the mean of a trait; fitness function is monotonically increasing or decreasing (p. 225).

q_stab_sel.label: Quantitative Stabilizing Selection
q_stab_sel.summary: Reduces variance without changing the mean; intermediate trait values have highest fitness (p. 225).

q_dis_sel.label: Quantitative Disruptive Selection
q_dis_sel.summary: Inflates variance; extreme trait values are favored over intermediate ones; often unstable unless maintained by negative frequency-dependent selection (p. 226).

multivariate_phenotype.label: Multivariate Phenotype and Correlational Selection
multivariate_phenotype.summary: Selection on combinations of traits rather than isolated characters (p. 226-227).

correlational_sel.label: Correlational Selection
correlational_sel.summary: Changes the bivariate distribution of traits without necessarily changing the means (p. 226).

epistatic_sel.label: Epistatic Correlational Selection
epistatic_sel.summary: Saddle-shaped fitness function where extreme combinations of traits are favored (p. 227).

ridge_sel.label: Ridge Correlational Selection
ridge_sel.summary: Fitness ridge where matching trait values are favored, leading to increased integration (p. 227).

indirect_selection_quant.label: Indirect Selection
indirect_selection_quant.summary: A trait experiences selection because it is correlated with another trait that is functionally related to fitness (p. 227-228).

genetic_correlations_quant.label: Genetic Correlations
genetic_correlations_quant.summary: Traits inherited together via pleiotropy or physical linkage, leading to correlated responses to selection (p. 228-229).

pleiotropy_def.label: Pleiotropy
pleiotropy_def.summary: Occurs when a single gene or group of genes influences variation in multiple traits (p. 228).

experimental_evolution.label: Responses to Selection: Experimental Populations
experimental_evolution.summary: Using controlled microbial cultures to investigate evolutionary processes in real-time (p. 230-236).

evo_rescue.label: Evolutionary Rescue
evo_rescue.summary: Survival of a population in lethal conditions via rapid adaptation, characterized by a U-shaped abundance trajectory (p. 231).

adaptation_rate.label: Rate of Adaptation
adaptation_rate.summary: Equal to the heritable variance of fitness (Fisher 1930). In finite populations, it depends on the supply of beneficial mutations, which increases with population size (p. 231).

sex_adaptation.label: Role of Sex in Adaptation
sex_adaptation.summary: Fusion and recombination accelerate adaptation in large populations by bringing together beneficial mutations from different lineages (p. 232).

gradual_vs_salt.label: Gradual vs. Saltational Adaptation
gradual_vs_salt.summary: While new mutations often have small effects, fixed beneficial mutations frequently have large effects (e.g., doubling fitness), contradicting a purely gradualist view (p. 232).

edam_process.label: EDAM Process
edam_process.summary: The sequence of adapting to new metabolic capabilities: Exaptation -> Deregulation -> Amplification -> Modification (p. 233).

adaptation_limits.label: Limits to Specialization
adaptation_limits.summary: Specialization is limited by functional interference (adaptation to one trait impairs another) and degradation through disuse (neutral loss of unused functions) (p. 236).

measuring_selection.label: Measuring Phenotypic Selection
measuring_selection.summary: The process of quantifying how specific phenotypes within a population influence survival and reproductive success.

phenotypic_selection_def.label: Phenotypic Selection Definition
phenotypic_selection_def.summary: Selection occurring when individuals with particular phenotypes survive and produce offspring at higher rates than others. Requires phenotypic variation and differential reproduction (p. 239).

selection_quantification.label: Quantifying Selection Strength
selection_quantification.summary: Methods for estimating the relationship between trait values (z) and fitness (w) using regression analysis.

linear_regression_selection.label: Linear Regression (Directional Selection)
linear_regression_selection.summary: Used when the fitness function is monotonic. Equation: w = a + bz, where 'a' is the y-intercept and 'b' is the slope measuring the strength of directional selection (p. 239).

quadratic_regression_selection.label: Quadratic Regression (Stabilizing/Disruptive)
quadratic_regression_selection.summary: Used when the fitness function has curvature. Equation: w = a + bz + (g/2)z^2. 'b' is the directional selection gradient; 'g' is the quadratic selection gradient measuring curvature (p. 239).

stabilizing_selection_fact.label: Stabilizing Selection
stabilizing_selection_fact.summary: Occurs when b ≈ 0 and g is significantly negative; fitness is highest at an intermediate phenotypic value (p. 239).

disruptive_selection_fact.label: Disruptive Selection
disruptive_selection_fact.summary: Occurs when b ≈ 0 and g is significantly positive; fitness function contains an intermediate performance minimum, favoring extreme phenotypes (p. 239).

standardized_selection.label: Standardized Selection Gradients
standardized_selection.summary: To allow comparisons across species/traits, gradients b and g are standardized by the trait's standard deviation to obtain bs and gs (p. 239).

modes_of_selection.label: Observed Patterns of Selection
modes_of_selection.summary: General trends in phenotypic selection observed in terrestrial plants, birds, lizards, frogs, and insects.

directional_trends.label: Directional Selection Trends
directional_trends.summary: Commonly acts on body size, typically favoring larger size associated with higher survival, fecundity, and mating success (p. 240).

fitness_component_differences.label: Fitness Component Divergence
fitness_component_differences.summary: Sexual selection (mating success) is frequently stronger and more consistent over time than viability selection (survival) (p. 240).

stabilizing_selection_paradox.label: Stabilizing Selection Paradox
stabilizing_selection_paradox.summary: Despite expectations for well-adapted populations, field studies provide little evidence for significant stabilizing selection compared to disruptive selection (p. 240).

paradox_tradeoffs.label: Fitness Trade-offs
paradox_tradeoffs.summary: A trait value increasing survival may decrease mating success or fecundity, reducing net selection (p. 240).

paradox_correlations.label: Genetic Correlations
paradox_correlations.summary: Direct selection on a trait may be balanced by opposing indirect selection on a correlated trait (p. 240).

paradox_temporal.label: Temporal Variation
paradox_temporal.summary: Directional selection may alternate in direction over time or space, reducing cumulative effects (p. 240).

microevolution_local_adaptation.label: Microevolution and Local Adaptation
microevolution_local_adaptation.summary: The study of rapid evolutionary change within populations and the process of adapting to local environments.

microevolution_def.label: Microevolution Definition
microevolution_def.summary: Detectable changes in the mean phenotype of a population within a few human generations (1 to 100 years) (p. 241).

drivers_of_rapid_evolution.label: Drivers of Rapid Microevolution
drivers_of_rapid_evolution.summary: Ecological conditions that accelerate evolutionary change.

colonization_events.label: Colonization Effects
colonization_events.summary: Colonizing new regions leads to newly adapted populations (e.g., D. subobscura size clines in Americas, Soapberry bug beak evolution in Florida) (p. 241).

anthropogenic_change.label: Anthropogenic Drivers
anthropogenic_change.summary: Human activities causing local adaptation to herbicides, heavy metals, insecticides, and climate change (e.g., flowering time shifts in plants) (p. 241).

divergent_selection.label: Divergent Selection
divergent_selection.summary: Directional selection acting in opposing directions in different populations, promoting local adaptation and speciation (p. 242).

abiotic_divergence.label: Abiotic Agents
abiotic_divergence.summary: Differences in soil chemistry, climate, or resources (e.g., plants on serpentine soils) (p. 242).

biotic_divergence.label: Biotic Agents
biotic_divergence.summary: Differences in interactions with predators, parasites, or competitors. Includes 'Character Displacement' where sympatric populations diverge to minimize competition (e.g., Galapagos finches) (p. 242).

sexual_divergence.label: Sexual Selection Agents
sexual_divergence.summary: Differing directions/strengths of sexual selection in populations, often due to differing light environments affecting sensory systems (e.g., benthic vs limnetic sticklebacks) (p. 242).

ecological_speciation.label: Ecological Speciation
ecological_speciation.summary: The evolution of reproductive barriers (prezygotic or postzygotic) as a consequence of ecologically based divergent selection (p. 243).

postzygotic_isolation_fact.label: Postzygotic Isolation
postzygotic_isolation_fact.summary: Hybrids have intermediate phenotypes that perform poorly in both parental environments, reducing gene flow (p. 243).

prezygotic_isolation_fact.label: Prezygotic Isolation
prezygotic_isolation_fact.summary: Individuals prefer mates with similar phenotypes (e.g., body shape), preventing inter-population mating (p. 243).

evolutionary_limits.label: Evolutionary Limits and Constraints
evolutionary_limits.summary: Factors that restrict the response of a population to selection, preventing adaptation despite intense selective pressure.

genetic_variation_limits.label: Genetic Variation Limits
genetic_variation_limits.summary: Selection cannot change a trait if there is no genetic variation. This is often measured by low heritability (p. 248).

dna_decay_fact.label: DNA Decay
dna_decay_fact.summary: Loss of gene functionality due to mutation accumulation when purifying selection is absent, creating fundamental limits (p. 248).

heritability_def.label: Heritability
heritability_def.summary: The proportion of phenotypic variation controlled by genetic factors, ranging from 0 (all environment) to 1 (all genetic) (p. 248).

tradeoffs_pleiotropy.label: Trade-offs and Pleiotropy
tradeoffs_pleiotropy.summary: Limits arising when the same gene affects multiple traits in opposing directions (Antagonistic Pleiotropy) (p. 249).

insect_development_tradeoff.label: Insect Development Trade-off
insect_development_tradeoff.summary: Alleles promoting fast development lead to early reproduction but result in smaller adult body size and reduced reproductive output (p. 249).

plant_flowering_tradeoff.label: Plant Flowering Trade-off
plant_flowering_tradeoff.summary: Early-flowering plants tend to produce smaller flowers and potentially fewer seeds (p. 249).

multivariate_selection.label: Multivariate Selection
multivariate_selection.summary: Constraints where genetic interactions among multiple traits prevent a response in the direction selection acts, even if individual traits show variation (e.g., Drosophila cuticular hydrocarbons) (p. 251).

gene_flow_constraints.label: Gene Flow Constraints
gene_flow_constraints.summary: Excessive gene flow from central to marginal populations can overwhelm local selection with non-adapted genotypes, retarding range expansion (p. 251).

modifier_genes_systems.label: Evolution of Modifier Genes and Biological Systems
modifier_genes_systems.summary: The study of genes that alter the biological system (transmission, ploidy, mutation rates) and how they evolve.

modifier_gene_def.label: Modifier Gene Definition
modifier_gene_def.summary: A gene whose alleles alter a feature of interest in a species, such as its mating system, mutation rate, or life history (p. 254).

selection_on_modifiers.label: Direct vs Indirect Selection
selection_on_modifiers.summary: Direct selection occurs when the modifier affects the carrier's fitness. Indirect selection occurs when the modifier alters the fitness of descendants (hitchhiking) (p. 256).

reduction_principle.label: The Reduction Principle
reduction_principle.summary: The theoretical prediction that in equilibrium under constant selection, biological systems evolve toward perfect transmission (zero mutation, recombination, etc.) (p. 257).

mutation_rate_evolution.label: Evolution of Mutation Rates
mutation_rate_evolution.summary: Asexuals evolve mutation rates maximizing lineage fitness. Sexuals evolve lower rates because sex/recombination separates beneficial mutations from the modifier, while costs (deleterious mutations) remain with the carrier (p. 258).

sex_recombination_evolution.label: Evolution of Sex and Recombination
sex_recombination_evolution.summary: Despite high costs (twofold cost of sex), sex is prevalent because it increases genetic variation, allowing the fittest individuals to be produced and spread the modifier genes (p. 258).

ploidy_evolution.label: Evolution of Ploidy
ploidy_evolution.summary: Haploidy is favored with low recombination or when beneficial alleles are recessive. Diploidy is favored in sexual populations to mask deleterious mutations (p. 259).

genotype_phenotype_map.label: The Genotype-Phenotype Map
genotype_phenotype_map.summary: The set of rules linking genomic information to the physical organism, focusing on plasticity and canalization.

reaction_norm_concept.label: Reaction Norm
reaction_norm_concept.summary: A property of a genotype where a trait is a continuous function of an environmental variable; it describes how development maps genotype to phenotype (p. 261).

adaptive_plasticity_fact.label: Adaptive Plasticity
adaptive_plasticity_fact.summary: Phenotypic changes triggered by environmental signals that improve reproductive success (e.g., Daphnia helmets in presence of predators) (p. 262).

canalization_concept.label: Canalization
canalization_concept.summary: The limitation of phenotypic variation by developmental mechanisms that buffer it against genetic and environmental variation (p. 261).

genetic_canalization.label: Genetic Canalization
genetic_canalization.summary: Buffering against genetic variation; mutations in genes affecting the trait are suppressed in the phenotype (p. 262).

environmental_canalization.label: Environmental Canalization
environmental_canalization.summary: Buffering against environmental variation; the phenotype remains constant regardless of environmental changes (p. 262).

life_history_evolution.label: Evolution of Life Histories
life_history_evolution.summary: The study of how organisms allocate resources over time to maximize fitness.

life_history_variables.label: Life History Variables
life_history_variables.summary: Composite of timing (age of reproduction) and resource allocation (growth, maintenance, storage, reproduction) (p. 269).

resource_allocation.label: Resource Allocation Trade-offs
resource_allocation.summary: Because resources are finite, increasing one allocation (e.g., growth) must decrease another (e.g., current reproduction) (p. 270).

r_k_selection.label: r and K Selection Theory
r_k_selection.summary: Framework describing selection based on population growth vs carrying capacity (p. 270).

r_selection_fact.label: r-selection
r_selection_fact.summary: Favors 'productivity' and rapid growth: early maturity, high fecundity, many small offspring, short life span (p. 271).

k_selection_fact.label: K-selection
k_selection_fact.summary: Favors 'persistence' near carrying capacity: delayed maturity, low reproductive investment, few large offspring, long life span (p. 271).

demographic_theory.label: Demographic Theory
demographic_theory.summary: Explains how mortality risk shapes evolution. High adult mortality risk favors earlier maturity and increased current reproduction (p. 271).

maturity_and_tradeoffs.label: Maturity and Investment Trade-offs
maturity_and_tradeoffs.summary: The balance between investment in growth, maintenance, and reproduction.

delayed_maturity_fact.label: Delayed Maturity Selection
delayed_maturity_fact.summary: Selection can favor delayed maturity and decreased reproductive investment to increase growth and maintenance, helping organisms outgrow size classes susceptible to predators. (p. 272)

pie_of_life_fact.label: The Pie of Life Trade-off
pie_of_life_fact.summary: Investment in reproduction is a trade-off against growth and maintenance; deferring reproduction allows for greater investment in other areas. (p. 272)

r_k_selection_fact.label: r- and K-selection Independence
r_k_selection_fact.summary: Alternative life histories resembling r- and K-selection can evolve independently of the population's proximity to carrying capacity, driven instead by survival probability as a function of age. (p. 272)

reproduction_strategies.label: Reproduction Strategies
reproduction_strategies.summary: The distinction between single and multiple reproductive events in a lifetime.

semelparity_concept.label: Semelparity
semelparity_concept.summary: A life history strategy where an organism reproduces once and then dies (e.g., Pacific salmon, agaves). (p. 272)

iteroparity_concept.label: Iteroparity
iteroparity_concept.summary: A life history strategy where an organism is capable of reproducing multiple times. (p. 272)

semelparity_evolution_fact.label: Evolution of Semelparity
semelparity_evolution_fact.summary: Semelparity is driven by the high cost of producing the first offspring (e.g., salmon swimming upstream); subsequent eggs are 'cheap,' making total investment until death more efficient. (p. 272)

offspring_allocation.label: Offspring Number versus Size
offspring_allocation.summary: The trade-off between producing many small offspring or few large offspring.

smith_fretwell_model.label: Smith and Fretwell Model
smith_fretwell_model.summary: Predicts optimal offspring number and size based on two assumptions: parent fitness increases with offspring number, and offspring survival increases with birth size. (p. 273)

guppy_offspring_fact.label: Guppy Offspring Trade-offs
guppy_offspring_fact.summary: Guppies in high-predation rivers (abundant food) produce many small offspring; guppies in headwater streams (scarce food) produce few large offspring because large offspring have a fitness advantage when food is scarce. (p. 273)

senescence_and_lifespan.label: Life Span and Senescence
senescence_and_lifespan.summary: The evolution of aging and the reduction of future survival to favor early reproduction.

senescence_definition.label: Definition of Senescence
senescence_definition.summary: An age-specific deterioration in function (e.g., reproductive ability) or an acceleration in death rate with age. (p. 273)

antagonistic_pleiotropy.label: Antagonistic Pleiotropy Model
antagonistic_pleiotropy.summary: Proposed by George Williams: Genes that increase reproductive investment early in life cause an earlier onset of senescence. (p. 273)

senescence_mortality_fact.label: Mortality and Life Span Evolution
senescence_mortality_fact.summary: High risk of external mortality (e.g., predation) selects for earlier maturity and high early reproductive investment, which offsets the cost of a reduced life span. (p. 273)

empirical_life_history_research.label: Empirical Life History Research
empirical_life_history_research.summary: Studies using comparative analyses and experimental evolution to validate life history theory.

fast_slow_continuum.label: Fast-Slow Continuum
fast_slow_continuum.summary: A gradient where 'fast' species mature early, produce many offspring, and are short-lived, while 'slow' species mature late, produce few well-provisioned offspring, and are long-lived. (p. 274)

peron_senescence_study.label: Peron et al. (2010) Study
peron_senescence_study.summary: Found that higher juvenile mortality, earlier first reproduction, and more early offspring predict earlier onset of senescence in birds and mammals. (p. 274)

rose_charlesworth_drosophila.label: Rose and Charlesworth Drosophila Experiment
rose_charlesworth_drosophila.summary: Selected for early vs late reproductive success; early-selection lines laid more eggs early but had shorter life spans, confirming trade-offs. (p. 274)

reznick_guppy_study.label: Reznick Guppy Field Experiments
reznick_guppy_study.summary: Guppies in high-predation (HP) environments mature earlier, allocate more to reproduction, and produce more/smaller offspring than low-predation (LP) guppies. (p. 274)

evolution_of_form_and_function.label: Evolution of Form and Function
evolution_of_form_and_function.summary: The relationship between morphological structure (form) and the tasks an organism performs (function) to achieve fitness.

form_performance_fitness_link.label: Form, Performance, and Fitness Link
form_performance_fitness_link.summary: Form shapes performance, and performance determines fitness. Natural selection acts on morphology because it affects the ability to survive and reproduce. (p. 276)

measuring_evolution_of_form.label: Measuring Evolution of Form
measuring_evolution_of_form.summary: Methods to quantify how form changes under selection.

population_level_analysis.label: Population-level Analysis
population_level_analysis.summary: Measuring natural selection within a population by comparing the form of survivors against the original sample using mark-recapture. (p. 277)

comparative_analysis_method.label: Comparative Analysis
comparative_analysis_method.summary: Using phylogenies to identify the sequence of assembly of complex adaptations across species. (p. 278)

mechanical_advantage_concept.label: Mechanical Advantage
mechanical_advantage_concept.summary: The ratio of input lever to output lever in muscle-skeleton systems. (p. 277)

mechanical_advantage_tradeoff.label: Force-Movement Trade-off
mechanical_advantage_tradeoff.summary: High mechanical advantage enhances force transmission but reduces movement transmission; low mechanical advantage does the opposite. (p. 277)

comparative_analyses_form.label: Comparative Analysis and Innovation
comparative_analyses_form.summary: Studying how complex innovations (e.g., powered flight) are assembled piecemeal over time. (p. 278)

bird_flight_assembly_fact.label: Assembly of Powered Flight
bird_flight_assembly_fact.summary: Bipedalism and feathers evolved long before powered flight; feathers initially evolved for insulation. (p. 278)

pharyngognathy_fact.label: Pharyngognathy in Fish
pharyngognathy_fact.summary: The evolution of a second set of jaws from gill arches. This innovation contributed to diversification in cichlids and labrids, but not in damselﬁshes. (p. 278)

functional_systems_constraints.label: Constraints on Functional Systems
functional_systems_constraints.summary: Factors that prevent an organism from reaching theoretical maximum performance.

multifunctionality_constraint.label: Multifunctionality Constraint
multifunctionality_constraint.summary: Structures often serve multiple roles (e.g., insect wings for flight, warmth, and camouflage), leading to trade-offs. (p. 279)

pleiotropy_constraint.label: Genetic Pleiotropy Constraint
pleiotropy_constraint.summary: Single genes contribute to many structures; modifying a gene for one morphological change may cause unintended negative changes elsewhere. (p. 279)

complexity_constraint.label: Complexity Constraint
complexity_constraint.summary: The number of parameters required to describe a form limits potential diversity. (p. 279)

decoupling_tradeoffs.label: Decoupling Trade-offs
decoupling_tradeoffs.summary: Overcoming constraints by breaking the linkage between performance traits.

functional_duplication_concept.label: Functional Duplication
functional_duplication_concept.summary: The emergence of a new structure that takes over a function, releasing the original structure from a trade-off. (p. 280)

pharyngeal_jaws_fact.label: Pharyngeal Jaws in Teleosts
pharyngeal_jaws_fact.summary: The evolution of a second set of jaws for prey processing released oral jaws to specialize in prey capture. (p. 280)

many_to_one_mapping.label: Many-to-One Mapping of Form to Function
many_to_one_mapping.summary: Multiple combinations of underlying morphological traits can produce the same functional outcome.

mapping_optimization_fact.label: Optimization of Multiple Properties
mapping_optimization_fact.summary: Many-to-one mapping allows an organism to optimize two functional properties by varying parameters that are neutral to one function but adaptive for another. (p. 280)

mapping_diversity_fact.label: Decoupled Morphological and Functional Diversity
mapping_diversity_fact.summary: Morphological diversity among species can be greater than functional diversity because many forms achieve the same function. (p. 281)

mapping_phylogenetic_signal_fact.label: Phylogenetic Signal in Design
mapping_phylogenetic_signal_fact.summary: Because many forms satisfy a function, lineages typically move to the closest form in morphospace rather than converging on a single ideal form. (p. 281)

biochemical_physiological_adaptations.label: Biochemical and Physiological Adaptations
biochemical_physiological_adaptations.summary: Evolutionary changes in biochemical processes and internal regulation to tolerate environmental extremes.

tolerance_vs_regulation.label: Tolerance versus Regulation
tolerance_vs_regulation.summary: Two primary strategies for dealing with abiotic stress.

tolerance_definition.label: Physiological Tolerance
